answer: Mandatory reciprocal random-audit pairing: each epoch a public beacon pairs every seat with a stranger who re-executes a sampled slice of its claimed work and posts the hash. A clone farm gets no haven, since holding fraction f of seats makes the odds both pairing ends are its own aliases only f-squared, so self-auditing demands owning nearly the whole network. Each seat locks a bond; honest reputation is patiently carved ivory, not a cheap dyed opal, and a caught mismatch slashes it. So 500 fakes cost 500 bonds and each round still risk a (1-f) draw of an honest auditor who exposes them.
